content.text: {"expertise":[{"text":"Unsupervised anomaly detection using autoencoders can learn normal Modbus traffic patterns from benign data alone and flag deviations without requiring labelled attack examples.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-10523","field":"abstract","quote":"leverages autoencoder-based neural networks trained exclusively on benign traffic to establish a baseline behavioural profile"}]},{"text":"Anomaly detection architectures for industrial control systems can maintain low false-positive rates in continuous operation while adapting to concept drift in network behaviour.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-10525","field":"abstract","quote":"capable of operating on highly specialised industrial protocols while maintaining low false-positive rates in continuous operation"}]},{"text":"Hybrid approaches combining specification-based rules with neural anomaly scoring achieve better balance than purely deep-learning systems for detecting protocol-level attacks in SCADA environments.","sources":[{"id":"SYN-PUB-10525","field":"abstract","quote":"hybrid architectures combining specification-based rules with neural anomaly scoring achieve the best overall balance"}]}],"fit":"strong","fitReason":"The researcher's work directly addresses the core challenge: unsupervised anomaly detection on Modbus networks [SYN-PUB-10523] using only benign traffic to establish normal baselines, achieving over 94% detection with false positives below 2%, and comparative evaluation of low-false-positive detection architectures suitable for continuous operational deployment [SYN-PUB-10525]."}
